businessRules.text: On create (POST), only `@type` is mandatory (userguide "Mandatory Attributes" table and conformance profile agree); a cart may be created empty or with any subset of `cartItem`, `contactMedium`, `relatedParty`, `validFor`.
PATCH must use JSON Merge (mandatory per conformance); only `cartItem`, `contactMedium`, `relatedParty` and `validFor` are patchable.

`cartTotalPrice`, `creationDate`, `lastUpdate`, `href`, `id`, `@baseType`, `@schemaLocation` and `@type` are non-patchable — `cartTotalPrice`, `creationDate` and `lastUpdate` are server-maintained, not client-supplied.
`cartTotalPrice` is the total of the cart "considering only Active cart items": items with `status = saveForLater` are not calculated in the cart prices (CartItem `status` description).
A cart references the customer via `relatedParty` (party or party role), or carries `contactMedium` instead when the customer is unknown/does not exist yet (prospect use case).

`cartItem.id` is identifier of the item within the cart, generally a sequence number (01, 02, 03, ...); `cartItemRelationship.id` refers to another cart item's `id` in the same cart (e.g. `relyOn`, `dependentOn`, `shipping`).

PATCH on `cartItem` is a merge-patch of the whole array: the userguide example passes the entire `cartItem` array to add a note to one existing item, and RFC 7386 merge-patch replaces arrays wholesale, so an item omitted from the array is removed.
When a PATCH creates new sub-resources, the same mandatory sub-resource attribute rules as POST apply (userguide PATCH description).

Conformance (response): `href` is mandatory in response messages; every present sub-resource requires `@type`, and nested refs require `id` (e.g. `cartItem.productOffering.id`, `cartItem.itemPrice.productOfferingPrice.id`, `relatedParty.partyOrPartyRole.id`); `cartItem.itemPrice`/`itemTotalPrice` require `priceType` and `price` when present.
Checkout (turning the cart into a draft product order) is described in the use cases but is not an operation of this API; it belongs to a TMF622 Product Ordering client, not this service.

Three notification events are declared (`Create`, `AttributeValueChange`, `Delete`) and the IR emits the same three listeners; there is no `StateChange` event and no `lifecycleStatus` field, consistent with the IR warning. The conformance profile marks no notification as mandatory.
Mandatory operations per conformance: GET, POST, DELETE; PATCH is optional but specified.
